title: Put the pieces of a recording in a different order
goal: You can cut a recording into pieces and throw one away, and that is where it stops: the pieces play in the order they were recorded and there is no way to change it. Showing the result before the setup, or moving a good take in front of a bad one, means recording again. The epic this belongs to is called cutting and arranging, and only the cutting half exists. Let somebody pick up a piece on the strip and drop it somewhere else in the order.
notes: Objective gap rather than a bug. The video-cutting epic is titled "Cutting and arranging: blade, trim, and place clips with confidence" and it has had exactly two tasks since the user answered "Start video now" on 2026-09-15: cutting into pieces, and keeping the pieces visible while trimming. Arranging is not built anywhere. Sources/PhotonzCore/VideoCuts.swift holds VideoCutList with split(atTimeline:), removePiece(at:) and keep(fromTimeline:), and no way to move a piece; the pieces array is in play order and timeline time is derived from it, so a move is a reorder of that array and everything downstream already reads through it. Sources/Photonz/TrimTimeline.swift draws the blocks. Filed with a card because dragging a piece to a new place is a new gesture on the strip that the user has not asked for by name, and the card also asks whether this is where video should go next at all.
acceptance: A piece can be picked up on the strip and dropped into a different place in the order, and the strip shows where it is going to land while you drag
What plays, what the playhead reads, and what comes out of an export all agree with the new order straight away
It is one undo step, and undo puts the piece back where it was
Nothing about a recording that was never reordered changes, including a saved file

Try it: Next release, turn on Cut a recording into pieces and drop the one you do not want (next-cut-a-recording), open a recording, press B twice to make three pieces, drag the last one to the front, and it plays first
A walk covers it, and it is named on the task with queue.mjs walks
anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar, and written into this task's log if it does not
